newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to lift 28.3-28.4 mln bls Iraq oil - official.
newsitem.headline: Russia to lift 28.3-28.4 mln bls Iraq oil - official.

text.p: Russian firms are scheduled to lift 28.3-28.4 million barrels of Iraqi crude in the $2 billion U.N. food-for-oil programme, an official at trader Zarubezhneft, which is coordinating the contracts, said on Thursday.

"The overall volumes due to be lifted by Russian companies has risen to 28.3-28.4 million barrels," said the official, who declined to be named. "This includes a number of extra spot contracts signed recently."
Yuri Agababov, deputy chief executive of Zarubezhneft, said separately that Russian companies had lifted 26.57 million barrels of Iraqi crude by May 15.
Russian companies had lifted 11.89 million barrels by March 14, at which point the expected total was 26.23 million barrels, up from the original total of 25.20 million.
Agababov said he did not expect Russian companies to sign any new contracts under the six-month programme which began in December 1996 and which is nearing completion.
"We do not expect to sign any new contracts (with Iraq) until Resolution 986 is extended by the U.N.," he said.
U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan has said he expects the Security Council to renew the oil sale agreement before June. Iraq is lobbying for $4 billion in oil sales, double its previous limit.
The Zarubezhneft official said eight Russian companies now had agreements to lift Iraqi crude.
Russian oil company Tatneft had joined the original list of seven Russian lifters when it signed a spot deal to take one million barrels of Iraqi crude, he said.
State oil company Rosneft and trading firms Zarubezhneft and Nafta-Moskva had also signed spot deals with Iraq in addition to volumes agreed in the original contracts, he added.
